narrative: The model estimated your chance of bad credit at 26%, meaning applicants with a similar profile are estimated to have about a one-in-four risk of credit problems; the bank’s decision threshold placed this estimate in the declined range. The three most influential factors, in order, were the requested credit length, your checking-account status, and your savings information. Your six-month requested term is much shorter than the approved average of about nineteen months, and this was the strongest factor; it moved the assessment toward lower risk. Your checking account being below zero DM was the second most important factor and pushed toward bad credit; only a small minority of approved applicants have that account status. Having no known savings was third and moved the assessment slightly toward lower risk. Although two of the top three factors were favorable, the checking-account signal and the rest of your profile left the overall risk estimate above the acceptance line. Next, bring the checking account into a non-negative position or provide a clear explanation, and supply verifiable savings information. It may also help to ask the bank whether a longer repayment term and additional affordability evidence would strengthen a new application.
